html:
A concubine of the Xianfeng Emperor who became the real ruler of Qing China for most of the half century from 1861 to her death in 1908.

She bore the emperor's only son. When Xianfeng died in 1861, she and his empress seized power from the regents in a palace coup and ruled for the boy, the Tongzhi Emperor. When he died young in 1875 she chose her nephew, the Guangxu Emperor, a small child, and kept ruling.

Her record is mixed:

  • She backed parts of the Self-Strengthening Movement.
  • In 1898 she crushed Guangxu's Hundred Days' Reform and kept him under house arrest.
  • In 1900 she backed the Boxer Rebellion against foreigners; foreign armies took Beijing and she fled.
  • Back in power, she began deep reforms, ending the old examinations in 1905 and planning a constitution.

Guangxu died the day before she did, probably poisoned. Her last choice of heir was the toddler Puyi. Older accounts painted her as a villain; recent historians are more divided.
sum: A concubine of the Xianfeng Emperor who became the real ruler of Qing China for most of the half century from 1861 to her death in 1908.
